title: A resolver whose incoming link goes down (MUTE_BLK keeps BUSY) outlives its call; stale legs later cut or re-point live calls

findings.title: A resolver whose incoming trunk's link goes down (LTU/MF8 MUTE_BLK) outlives its call. Its stale legs are later cut, re-pointed or re-seized.
findings.mechanism:
When a local trunk's link dies, local_trunk.v:188-189 drops A and raises MUTE_BLK, and port.v:147 makes MUTE_BLK part of every port's BUSY.

R_GONE fires only when the incoming reads BUSY=0 (net_unit.v:688-689), so it cannot fire for the whole outage. Meanwhile the incoming's latch released itself T_REL after its A fell, and every leg released itself (their E fell).

The resolver keeps rs_busy, rs_held and rs_leg:
- Its old legs stay `mine` (:435-436).
- R_LEG still fires on ANY M on an old leg (:684-687). w_res then drops the other old legs and writes the way back onto the dead incoming (:691-705).
- At the mend, R_GONE drops every old leg (:694-698).

All of these writes land on ports that other calls now use.
findings.trigger:
tb_fx sc2, real timers. A W neighbour's seizure on LTU channel B10 is forwarded into E30 and S40. Then the LTU cable is cut for longer than 256 ms.
- var0: during the outage B20 keys 1; its flood takes E30 and S40, the free old legs. The cable is mended while B20 is dialling.
- var1: during the outage the E neighbour seizes E30 to call B21. The cable is mended during that call.
findings.consequence:
The resolver is lost for the whole outage; with NRES=2 that is half of a transit's forwarding.

var0: at the mend the stale R_GONE re-points B20's two live trunks to 00, cutting its flood mid-dial. When the E party claims anyway, B20 hears it but the E party hears nothing. B's classifier then takes the E party's claim level on the now non-BUSY E30 as a fresh incoming seizure, monitors it and floods it W and S: a phantom flood.

var1: the stale R_LEG re-points the dead B10 at E30. After the mend the W neighbour sees a seizure on its channel 0 carrying the E caller's hook and voice for the whole E-B21 call. A real W neighbour would hold it, monitor it and forward it through its own network for the call's duration; nothing times out a steady M at a monitor or a resolver.

Everything heals only when the unrelated call ends.
findings.realistic: Real timers, as run. It needs any LTU or MF8 outage longer than T_REL (256 ms) that starts while a forward from that link is held. That probability is roughly the link's forward occupancy at the transit: ~5-25% of such outages at a busy hub. var1 is the likely outcome once the old legs are reused before the mend. A baseband cut has no MUTE and is not affected.
findings.evidence:
All logs are under work/audit/fwd/.

run_fx_sc2var0.log:
- :31: the forward.
- :41: link down at 90 ms.
- :54-57: B10 and the legs release at 346 ms.
- :59: FAIL, the resolver is still held.
- :75-77: B20 takes 30 and 40.
- :97: mended at 2050 ms.
- :106-108 '2050.141 rs_busy 01 -> 00 / 2050.425 port 40 latch -> src 00 bsy 0 / 2050.559 port 30 latch -> src 00': the stale drops.
- :114-115: FAIL.
- :124-139: E30 re-classified and forwarded; '4742.399 far LTU ch 0: M seen by W neighbour -> 1'.
- :145-147: FAIL.

run_fx_sc2var1.log:
- :64-65 '500.395 rs_busy 01 -> 00 / 500.813 port 10 latch -> src 30 bsy 1': the stale R_LEG and way back.
- :115 '4630.009 far LTU ch 0: M seen by W neighbour -> 1'.
- :117-119: FAIL for the phantom M and the voice leak.
- :120, :124: it clears only when the E call ends.

With the fix:
- runfix_fx_sc2var0.log: 18/18 pass; '346.520 rs_busy 01 -> 00'.
- runfix_fx_sc2var1.log: all pass except one bench-check artefact. The check expected E30 to listen to 00, but B's one-leg forward correctly re-points E30 at S40.
- Regressions on the fix: runfix_fx_sc4.log PASS, runfix_chain.log 32/32 PASS, runfix_lchain.log 48/48 PASS.
findings.fix:
Implemented in work/audit/fwd/rtl_fix/net_unit.v:
- Two flip-flops per leg: rs_lb (seen BUSY) and rs_lf (then seen free, meaning it released itself).
- A resolver whose held legs are all rs_lf dissolves without writing anything.
- rs_lf legs are excluded from R_LEG, from the w_res and w_claim drops, and from `mine`.

Cost: about 8 flip-flops and a few gates per resolver, roughly 2 packages. It also removes the normally redundant R_GONE writes to legs that have already released.
